newsitem.title: RUSSIA: ROUBLE SHORTAGE PUSHES RUSSIAN T-BILL YIELDS UP.
newsitem.headline: ROUBLE SHORTAGE PUSHES RUSSIAN T-BILL YIELDS UP.

text.p: Yields on Russian GKO discount Treasury bills broke resistance levels on Wednesday as a severe cash shortage prompted low bids and poor demand at auction, dealers said.

"The shortage of roubles is continuing. Everyone bid low and was right," said Tokobank dealer Vadim Kononov. "Both auctions were difficult for the Finance Ministry because of aggressive bids and lack of demand."
A new resistance level of 19.30 percent on the secondary market was set after previous resistance of 19.00 percent was breached during Wednesday's auction.
Dealers said the new levels could make the secondary market unstable in the next few days amid a shortage of roubles.
The highest accepted yield on an issue of 364-day T-bill was 19.27 percent while the 182-day T-bill topped out at 19.33 percent.
Dealers said the current yield level was to high and indicated the Finance Ministry would struggle to find the cash needed to repay maturing issues.
A dealer said it was easy for the Ministry to understand how much money came to the auctions, unlike when OFZ bonds were sold.
"In this situation the size of the premium alerts people because we have been standing by the 19 percent level for too long," he said.
He forecast a shaky market in the next few days as local banks declined to free up fresh funds due to high overnight credit rates.
"It takes a couple of days for non-residents to pour in money for the new yield level," he said.

"We shall survive these days and I do not think anyone will start selling actively. Maybe some operators would like to reshuffle their portfolios from OFZs to middle-term T-bills as tomorrow the yield may reach 18.5 percent annual."

Dealers said low demand from Russian banks was due to a shortage of roubles on the interbank market, while foreign investors were waiting for the autumn, when Russia's international credit rating may be upgraded.
